paragraphs: Mentioned in [Chullin 136a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.136a.17); the text there at [87b](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.87b.9) reads R' Assi of Naharbil, but Dikdukei Soferim reads R' Yosi.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The first linked passage names Rabbi Yosi of Naharbil in a discussion of priestly gifts. The second names Rabbi Assi of Naharbil in a discussion of blood. Hyman gives Naharbal in the heading and reports a Yosi variant for 87b.

Dikdukei Soferim’s Yosi reading is attributed by Hyman, not a new collation. Naharbal/Naharbil and Yosi/Assi remain distinct supplied forms. Initial mem is read locatively, without geographic identification or silent name harmonization. All three personal title abbreviations remain R'.
